title: Activity Log
text: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The Activity Log tab contains the history of changes related to the selected guest. Activity Log \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The log displays the date and time of the change, the employee or system that performed the action, the type of change, and related details. For example, the log records tags being added or removed, changes to notes, preferences, and RFM Status. Data Filtering Activity Log Filter \[\[delimiter rows=1]] To filter the Activity Log, click Filters. After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Selected filters are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The filters are reset after you log out. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Create and Edit
text: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Creating an RFM Status To create a new RFM Status, click Edit, then Add RFM Status, fill in the fields, and click Add. Create RFM Status \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Status Name Color Description Recency (R) — determines how long ago the guest's last order should have been to match the status. If All Time is enabled, the day limit is removed and the guest's entire order history is included in the calculation. Frequency (F) — determines the minimum number of orders the guest must make during the selected period. Monetary (M) — determines the minimum amount the guest must spend during the selected period. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] After an RFM Status is created, the system automatically recalculates RFM and distributes guests according to the current rules. \[\[/info]] Editing an RFM Status After clicking Edit, the page switches to edit mode. Edit RFM Status \[\[delimiter rows=1]] On the editing page, you can make the following changes: Calculation Horizon. Specify the period in days used to calculate Frequency and Monetary. After the new settings are applied, the number of guests in the RFM Statuses will be recalculated. Changing Priority. Change the priority of RFM Statuses by dragging and dropping the rows. If a guest meets the conditions of several statuses at the same time, the status with the higher priority will be assigned. Adding an RFM Status. Editing an RFM Status. Click the row of the required RFM Status to change its parameters. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] After the changes are saved, the system automatically recalculates RFM and distributes guests according to the current rules. \[\[/info]] Deleting an RFM Status Click Edit. Right-click the required RFM Status. Select Delete RFM Status. Confirm the deletion. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] After an RFM Status is deleted, the system automatically recalculates RFM and distributes guests according to the current rules. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Create and Edit Manual Tags
text: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Creating a Manual Tag Group To create a new Manual Tag group: Click Create. Fill in the group settings. Click Save. Create Manual Tag Group \[\[delimiter rows=1]] 1\. Name 2\. Locations 3\. Description 4\. Editable in Reservations — allows you to assign and remove tags from this group directly in the reservation system. 5\. Available in Waiter App — allows you to use tags from this group in the Waiter App. Assign to Guest — allows you to assign and remove tags from this group in the Waiter App. This setting becomes available only when Available in Waiter App is enabled. 7\. Available in Reservation Widget — allows you to display tags from this group in the Reservation Widget. When this setting is enabled, you can specify a public group name that will be displayed in the widget. 8\. Reservations Display — allows you to choose where the group tags will be displayed: in the guest profile, time slot, on the table, in the call widget, in the guest hint, and in the Reservation List. Creating a Tag To add a tag to a group: Click Add Tag. Fill in the tag settings. Click Add. Click Save for the changes to take effect. Create Tag \[\[delimiter rows=1]] 1\. Name 2\. Short Name 3\. Color 4\. Icon 5\. Hint Text Editing To change the settings of a group or its Manual Tags, open the required group, make the changes, and click Save. Deleting a Manual Tag Group To delete a Manual Tag group, open the actions menu in the group list or on the group page and select Delete. Confirm the deletion in the window that opens. When a group is deleted, all tags in the group are deleted and removed from all guests they were assigned to. Deleting a Manual Tag To delete a Manual Tag, open the tag group, remove the required tag from the list, and click Save. After deletion, the tag will be removed from all guests it was assigned to. \[\[delimiter rows=5]]

title: Create Guest
text: To create a new guest: Go to Marketing → Guests Click Create Enter the guest details Click Create Create Guest \[\[delimiter rows=1]] 1\. First Name 2\. Last Name 3\. Sex 4\. Birthday 5\. Email 6\. Telegram 7\. Phone Number/Card Number By default, a guest is identified by their phone number. To use a card number for identification, click Card Number, then enter the card number. If a card number is entered, a phone number cannot be added. Edit Guest To edit a guest, use one of the following methods: Open the guest profile, click the button with the colon icon, and select Edit In the guest table, right-click the required guest and select Edit from the context menu Make the required changes and click Save. Colon Button Phone Numbers A guest profile can contain multiple phone numbers. Phone numbers can be edited, and one of them can be set as the primary number for communication with the guest. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The phone number associated with a loyalty card cannot be changed. \[\[/info]] When a new phone number is added, the system checks whether it is already used in another guest profile. If the number is already in use, a warning will appear. If confirmed, the guest profile that previously used this number will be deactivated. Phone Number Already in Use \[\[delimiter rows=1]] If a guest changes their phone number and wants to keep their bonus points and loyalty level: Add the new phone number to the guest profile as an additional number Ask the guest to register in the loyalty system using the new number After registration, set the new number as the primary number Bonus points and loyalty level will be automatically synchronized with the new card. If the guest has already registered in the loyalty system using the new number: In this case, a second guest profile may appear in the system. To combine the data into one profile: Open the guest profile with the old phone number Add the new number as an additional number Confirm the deactivation of the second profile in the warning that appears Set the new number as the primary number As a result, only one active guest profile will remain, and the bonus points and loyalty level will be synchronized. Deactivated Guest A guest profile is deactivated if its phone number is added to another profile. In this case, the phone number will be associated with the new profile, and the bonus points and loyalty level will be synchronized with the new card. After deactivation, the profile remains available for viewing, but its data cannot be edited. A deactivated guest is not included in the RFM calculation. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Creating a Reservation
text: Methods of Creating a Reservation You can create a reservation in two main ways. This helps you choose the most convenient option depending on the situation and speeds up work with the functionality. 1\. Button +Add Reservation Click the +Add Reservation button in the upper right corner of the screen. In the opened sidebar specify the guest. Select one or more tables. If necessary, edit the interval or reservation date. Fill in the remaining fields — number of guests, comment, reservation source, tags. Disable or keep SMS notification about the reservation. To save the reservation click Save. 2\. Selecting a Time Interval on the Timeline Find a suitable time and table on the timeline. Click on the timeline cell. A single click will open the sidebar to set up the reservation. Click and drag right or left will immediately set the required reservation duration. Dragging up or down will allow you to select multiple tables. In the opened sidebar specify the guest. Add tables or if necessary change the selected table. If necessary, edit the interval or reservation date. Fill in the remaining fields — number of guests, comment, reservation source, tags. Disable or keep SMS notification about the reservation. To save the reservation click Save. Sidebar When you select any of the methods, a sidebar opens. It is here that all information about the reservation is filled in. In the panel you can add or change a guest, select or change a table, specify an interval, number of guests, add a comment and see the reservation change history. The reservation source, status and SMS sending parameters are also indicated there. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] To create a reservation, it is enough to specify a guest and a table, the remaining fields will be filled in by default. \[\[/info]] 1\. Guest When you click on a guest, a second sidebar opens, which allows you to: Find a guest by phone number, name or loyalty card Not add a specific guest to the reservation Create a new guest and add them to the reservation Creating a Guest To create a new guest, you need to specify the following data: Name (Last name is not required) Phone number Gender \[\[delimiter rows=1]] \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] More about creating a guest can be read in this article. \[\[/info]] 2\. Table Selection {#multireserve} Allows you to select one or more tables. A reservation with 2 or more tables is called multi-reservation. This type of reservation has a limitation: time gaps between reservations on different tables are not allowed. More about multi-reservations can be read in article. To specify multiple tables, in the opened sidebar: Enable Select multiple tables. Find suitable tables in the list, you can also search for tables by name, filter tables by needed criteria and sort the list. Select the required tables, then click Apply. 3\. Reservation Date and Start Time Start time is a multiple of 15-minute intervals. By default, when creating a reservation by button, the nearest time that is a multiple of 15 minutes is specified. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] For example, it is now 18:12, when creating a reservation, time 18:15 will be specified. \[\[/info]] 4\. Duration Reservation duration is also a multiple of 15 minutes. By default, when creating using the +Add Reservation button, 2 hours is specified. 5\. Number of Guests You can quickly specify up to 10 guests, or manually specify a larger company. By default, one guest is specified. To specify a company of more than 10 people, click 10+ and enter the required number manually. 6\. Reservation Source Specifying the reservation source will allow you to then analyze where guest reservations come from. This helps you understand which channels work better and which ones work worse, so you can evaluate their effectiveness and optimize guest acquisition. Available reservation sources: Phone call (Selected by default) Walk-in guest Messenger Website 7\. Reservation Tags Reservation tags help you manually mark reservations. With their help you can visually highlight important records, quickly understand the context of a reservation, group reservations and find them using filters. More about creating and using tags can be read in this article. 8\. Comment In the comment you can specify any necessary information about the reservation. 9\. Reservation Status It shows whether the reservation is confirmed or if the guest cancelled it. You can select it only manually in the sidebar when creating or editing a reservation. Three statuses are available when creating a reservation: Confirmed (Selected by default when creating a reservation for today) Not confirmed (Selected by default when creating a reservation for a future date) In progress \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] There are a total of five statuses for reservations. More about statuses can be read in this article. \[\[/info]] 9\. SMS Notification If a reservation is created for the future, after selecting a guest you can choose to send an SMS notification. The SMS template is configured separately in the Reservations - Settings section. By default, this option is active. \[\[delimiter rows=3]] Read further: — Automatic check creation from reservation \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: How to create a reservation. Description of fields

title: Creating and Configuring a Survey
text: The builder allows you to assemble a survey from pages and questions, configure the completion scenario and design the form for the respondent. To create a draft, you must fill in the required fields of the basic information and add at least one question. Creating a Survey Open the Surveys section. Click Create. On the Details step, specify the name and location. On the Questions step, configure the survey structure. If necessary, configure transitions between survey stages on the Conditions step. If necessary, change the appearance on the Design step. Click Create on the last step. After a successful save, the system will create a survey with the status Draft. The Distribution section will become available on the survey page, and the Save button will replace the Create button. Step 1. Details \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Name Location Step 2. Questions At this step, the survey structure is formed. You can add, delete and duplicate pages and questions, as well as change their order. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Page Types Page with questions Use a page with questions to collect answers. One page can contain one or more questions, and all its content is displayed to the respondent at once. Start screen The start screen is displayed before the questions and there can only be one. It can be used for a welcome message, explaining the purpose of the survey, or obtaining consent for the processing of personal data. On the start screen, you can add text and variables, add an image, enable consent for the processing of personal data, and add the ability to unsubscribe from survey mailings. Information screen An information screen can be placed between pages with questions. It does not require a response and is suitable for instructions, explanations or visual inserts. You can add text, variables and an image to the screen. Final screen The final screen completes the completion scenario. A survey can have several final screens, for example for different branches of the scenario. On the final screen, you can add text, variables, an image and the ability to unsubscribe from survey mailings. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] If a survey has several final screens and transition conditions are not configured, the respondent is shown the first final screen in order. \[\[/info]] Consent for Processing of Personal Data This setting is only available on the start screen. Enable Consent to continue. Specify a link to the privacy policy. Save the changes. The respondent will see a required consent checkbox. Until the checkbox is checked, the Start button will be unavailable. Unsubscribing from Survey Mailings This setting can be added to the start or final screen. After confirming the unsubscription, the guest is excluded from further survey mailings. For respondents who opened the survey via an anonymous link, this block is not displayed. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] If the survey is opened via a public anonymous link, personal variables are not displayed. \[\[/info]] You can add and manage the order of survey pages at the top of the form. Click on the 2 dots on the page type, or drag manually by holding the 6 dots on the page type. General Question Settings The following basic parameters are available for questions: Question type — determines the answer format: Rating, NPS, Choice or Input. Required — if enabled, the respondent will not be able to continue or submit the survey without an answer. This setting is enabled by default. Question text — a required field of up to 250 characters. Explanation — additional text under the question of up to 250 characters. Rating The Rating type is used for a quantitative assessment of the visit, service or another indicator. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Available settings: Display type — Stars or Numbers. Include in guest statistics — allows the rating to be used in auto-tag conditions and is included in guest statistics. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] If a response has several Rating type questions with the guest statistics setting enabled, the system uses the average value of these ratings for this response. \[\[/info]] NPS The NPS type is used to assess a guest's willingness to recommend the establishment. It is rated on a scale from 1 to 10. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Choice The Choice type allows you to offer the respondent ready-made answer options. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Available settings: Choice type — Single or multiple choice. Answer options Other answer — adds an option, upon selection of which the respondent enters their own text. For the custom option, you can change the name and configure the requirement and length of the entered text. Input The Input type is used for text responses and contact data. Within one question, you can add several fields, for example name, phone and comment. All filled-in fields are saved as one answer to the question. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Available for each field: Title Required Mask — determines the format and validation rules for the entered value. Available masks: Text, First name, Last name, Phone, Email. Step 3. Conditions Conditions allow you to change the sequential completion of the survey and direct the respondent to different pages depending on the answer. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] If conditions are not configured, pages are shown sequentially. How to Configure a Transition Open the Conditions step. Find the required question. Click Add condition. Select the respondent's behavior. Select the target page in the Transition field. If necessary, add other conditions. Available conditions: On answer selection — works for Rating, NPS and Choice questions. Specify one or more values for which the transition should occur. Always — the transition occurs regardless of the answer. On skip — triggers if the respondent did not answer. Only available for a non-required question. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] A transition can only be configured forward: the target page must be located after the current one. This eliminates scenario looping. \[\[/info]] If several conditions are configured for a question, the system checks them from top to bottom and executes the first matching condition. When changing the structure, take the following into account: If you move the target page before the current one, the transition will become invalid and will need to be reconfigured; If you make a question required, the On skip condition for it will be reset; When a page is deleted, transitions to it are cleared; When a question is deleted, conditions related to it are deleted. Step 4. Design The Design section changes only the appearance of the web form and does not affect the survey completion logic. The form automatically adapts to mobile devices and computers. The width of the content is determined by the system. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Available settings: Color of background, fields, buttons, accent elements and text; Logo; Link that redirects when the logo is clicked; Background image; Background image darkening. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Creating a survey, configuring questions, screens, transition conditions and appearance.

title: Editing and Canceling a Reservation
text: You can edit a reservation in several ways: through the sidebar, timeline, floor plan or reservations table. Through the Sidebar Click on a reservation on the timeline. In the opened sidebar make changes: guest, table, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. Click Save to apply the changes. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The sidebar also has Reservation Change Log. \[\[/info]] Using the Timeline Select a reservation on the timeline. Click and hold the reservation again. Drag the reservation to another table or another time. If necessary, add an additional table by selecting it on the timeline. Click Save to apply the changes. In the Floor Plan Section Select a reservation in the left sidebar (for convenience you can filter the list by table by selecting it on the floor plan). If necessary, select a table on the floor plan to show only its reservations. In the opened sidebar make changes: guest, table, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. Click Save to apply the changes. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] By selecting a table with an In progress reservation on the floor plan, you can quickly change the status or edit the reservation time by 15 minutes. \[\[/info]] In the Reservations Table Click on a reservation in the list. In the opened sidebar make changes: guest, table, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. Click Save to apply the changes. Editing Multi-Reservations In a multi-reservation you can: Edit all tables simultaneously. Edit individual tables independently. To exclude a table from editing, click on it. 1\. If All Tables Are Selected: Increasing or decreasing time on one slot will affect all associated tables. The sidebar allows editing of guest, date and time, number of guests, tags, comment, status. It is possible to add additional tables by selecting them on the timeline or specifying through the sidebar. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Editing time of a multi-reservation through the sidebar is only available if the start and end times are the same for all tables. \[\[/info]] 2\. If One Table Is Selected: Increase or decrease time on this table, remembering the limitations. In the sidebar, start time and duration can be edited for each individual table. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Even if only one table is selected, changing the guest, number of guests, tags, comment or status changes apply to the entire reservation. \[\[/info]] Blocking Reservation Changes Blocking prohibits changing guest and table. Any user can remove the block at any time. To block a reservation: Click Do not change. After blocking, hover over the button to see the blocking time and the user who set the block. Canceling a Reservation To cancel a reservation: Set status to Cancelled. Select the reason for cancellation. After cancellation, the reservation is automatically moved to the Archive section. \[\[delimiter rows=3]] Read further: — Reservation Statuses \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Capabilities when editing a reservation.

title: Editing and Managing a Survey
text: Editing a Survey Surveys with the statuses Draft, Published and Unpublished can be edited if you have the appropriate permissions. A deactivated survey is available for viewing only. Restrictions After Receiving Responses If the survey has no responses yet, the structure can be edited without restrictions. If at least one response has been received, some parameters are locked so as not to change the type of already saved data. Changes to a published survey apply to new completions, including via previously sent links. Already received responses are retained. After receiving responses, you cannot change: The question type; The field mask in an Input type question; The choice type Single or Multiple in a Choice type question. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Open the survey. Change the necessary parameters. Click Save. If the survey is published, confirm the change to the published form. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Text changes are not stored as a separate historical version: current names of questions, fields and options are displayed in old responses. When a new field or option is added, it is not present in old responses, and deleted elements are retained in those responses where they had already been filled in. \[\[/info]] Duplicating a Survey \[\[delimiter rows=1]] When duplicating, the system creates a new survey with the status Draft and copies the basic information, questions and pages, transition conditions and design settings. Publication settings and responses are not copied. To duplicate a survey: Open the context menu of the required survey by right-clicking on the required survey in the list. Or open the survey page. Select the duplication action. The system will open the creation form and fill it with data from the original survey. Make the necessary changes. Click Save. Deactivating and Deleting a Survey \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Deactivation is used if a previously published survey should no longer be returned to use. You can deactivate a survey with the status Published or Unpublished. Deletion is available for a survey with the status Draft. After confirmation, the draft is deleted from the list. To Deactivate/Delete a survey: Open the context menu of the required survey by right-clicking on the required survey in the list. Or open the survey page. Select the action Delete or Deactivate. Confirm the action. For previously published surveys, use unpublishing or deactivation depending on whether you plan to return the survey to use. After deactivation: The status changes to Deactivated; Links become unavailable; The survey cannot be connected to a mailing; The survey opens only in view mode; editing and republishing are unavailable. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Deactivation is irreversible. Use unpublishing for a temporary stop. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Editing, deactivating, deleting and duplicating a survey.

title: Exporting Responses
text: Export allows you to download survey results for additional analysis in spreadsheets or BI systems. Data can be exported from the responses of a specific survey or from the general Responses table. General Export Rules When exporting, the system takes into account the current view of the table. The columns exported are those selected in the column display settings, and their order. The applied sorting and active filters are taken into account. The Text Responses and Ratings columns are used only in the table interface and are not included in the export. Instead, the system exports detailed answers to the questions. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The detailed block always preserves the structure of the survey questions. If a question was not shown to the respondent due to conditions, or the answer is missing, the corresponding value remains empty. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Exporting Responses for a Single Survey Open a survey from the list of surveys Click View responses Click the export button If the export is performed from the Responses tab of a specific survey: Each question is exported into a separate column; The column name becomes the text of the question; Questions are arranged in the same order as in the survey; Values for each question are filled in the response row. This format is convenient to use when you need to compare respondents' answers to the same set of questions. Exporting the General Responses Table \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Open the section Feedback -> Responses Set filtering and other table parameters Click the export button If the export is performed from the general Responses table: The survey name is added to the export; Questions and answers are output through the Question and Answer fields; The export takes into account the selected filters by period, locations, surveys and other parameters. This option is suitable for analyzing data across several surveys at once. Response Format by Question Type Rating and NPS — a numeric value is exported. Input — the entered text is exported. If a question has several fields, their values are saved together. For specialized fields, for example first name, last name or phone number, the field name and the entered value are specified. Choice — the selected options are exported. If the respondent used Custom option, its text is also included in the value. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Deleted responses are not included in the export. \[\[/info]]
description: Rules for exporting responses for a single survey and from the general Responses table.

title: Floor Plan
text: Floor plan is a visual representation of the establishment's tables, which allows you to assess the hall occupancy and manage reservations tied to specific tables. The section displays the status of tables for the selected date and time. The color and additional information on the table depend on the reservation status and the selected display mode. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The state of the plan depends on the selected time. When switching time slots, the system updates the statuses of tables and information about related reservations. By default, the sidebar displays a list of all reservations and their statuses from all tables at the current time. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Main elements: Table plan — shows the location of tables, their capacity and current state. Reservations sidebar — displays reservations of the selected table or a general list of reservations. Time panel — determines the status of tables at the selected moment. Button to create a reservation Floor or zone selection — switches the displayed part of the establishment. Display settings — configures the information in tooltips next to tables and plan display. Each table displays: Number or name; Maximum capacity; Deposit indicator, if any. How the floor plan takes into account the selected time \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The time panel is divided into 15-minute intervals. The minimum reservation duration is 15 minutes and must be a multiple of 15 minutes. \[\[/info]] The selected time affects: The color and state of tables; Information in the placards next to tables; Selection of reservations for editing; Start time when creating a reservation. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Clicking on a table filters the list of reservations in the left sidebar only by the selected table. \[\[/info]] Table States Color designations of table status are similar to the general status model with some additions. Main statuses on the floor plan: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Yellow — in status "Confirmed" Orange — in status "Not confirmed" Green — in status "In progress" Pink — in status "Not confirmed", if guest is late Light blue — in status "Confirmed", if guest is late Unique display for floor plan: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Table is free Table lock Collision - intersection with an existing reservation on this table Viewing reservations of the selected table \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Select a date and time. Click on the required table. The sidebar will show a list of reservations for this table for the selected day. Select a reservation card to view detailed information and available actions. Reservations in the sidebar are grouped by statuses. A started reservation is displayed first. Quick actions are available for a started reservation: Change the duration of the reservation −15 minutes — decrease duration +15 minutes — increase duration Change reservation status - click on the status dropdown list to select Move guests - open menu to transfer the reservation to another table. Read more about moving below in this article. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The name of the selected table is displayed at the top of the sidebar. Click on it to open information about the table, including its blocking periods for the selected day. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] To return to the general list of reservations, click on a free area of the plan or deselect the table. \[\[/info]] Guest Information When you hover over a placard with the guest's name, you can see additional information about the guest. The tooltip displays 5 tags. The full list of tags is available in the guest profile. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Configuring the Display of Information About Tables The display panel controls the content of information placards next to tables. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The following modes are available: Guest — first and last name of the guest of the current reservation. If there is no current reservation, the placard is not displayed. Reservations — up to three reservations: current and two next or three next. Past reservations are not displayed in the placard. Time shows: Time until the end of the current reservation Time until the start of the next reservation, if there is no current one Time overdue after the start of an unconfirmed or confirmed reservation, if guests have not yet arrived. Money — the amount of the current reservation's check. Waiter — name and last name of the waiter from the current reservation's check. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] If there is no data for the selected mode, the placard next to the table is not displayed. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Configuring Objects on the Plan In the plan settings you can hide or show additional objects. Constructions - walls, windows, doors, stairs. Interior - speakers, televisions, outlets, text labels and chair display. Details - when activated, optimizes this section for devices with low performance or low internet speed. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Changes are applied immediately after switching the setting and are saved after page reload. After fully logging out of the account, settings may be reset. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Creating a Reservation You can create a reservation on the floor plan in several ways: Click the + button after selecting a time; Select a table and click the + button; Open the context menu of the table (right-click) and select Create reservation. Creating a Reservation Select time on the scale. Click +. The selected table will be automatically entered in the form. Fill in the reservation form. All fields for creating a reservation are described in more detail in this article. If necessary, select a table. If the table was not selected, suitable tables for the specified time will be highlighted on the floor plan. Check the duration and other reservation fields. Save the changes. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Clicking on a table does not create a reservation. It opens a list of reservations for the selected table. \[\[/info]] Overlapping Reservations The system can save multiple reservations for one table at overlapping times. Such an overlap is called a collision. When creating or changing a reservation, the system warns of an overlap, but does not block saving. A collision is displayed on the table with a separate visual state. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Before saving, check the time and selected table. A collision means that multiple reservations claim the same table at the same time period. \[\[/info]] Editing a Reservation Select the reservation you are interested in from the sidebar (for convenience, you can filter the list by table by selecting it on the floor plan). Change the necessary parameters. Save the changes. Editing is performed in the standard reservation form. In it you can change the time, duration, table and other available parameters. More about editing reservations can be read in this article. Moving Guests {#replace} For a started reservation, you can move guests to another table. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Click Move in the card of the started reservation or right-click on the table with the required reservation at this moment. Select the move action. Specify a full transfer of the reservation or a transfer from a specific time. Select a new table. Check the preview result and possible overlaps. Confirm the move. If there are associated checks, the system initiates their transfer to the new table.

title: General Information
text: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Manual Tags allow you to manually mark guests and store information that should be taken into account when providing service. For example, they can be used to identify VIP guests, dietary restrictions, preferences, or special service requirements. Manual Tags are used in several sections of the system: ✔ Reservations — tags can be displayed in the guest profile, on the reservation timeline, and on the floor plan tables, depending on the group settings. If editing is enabled, tags can be assigned and removed directly from a reservation ✔ Guests — tags are displayed in the guest list and guest profile, where they can be assigned and removed ✔ Waiter App — tags can be viewed and assigned to guests if this is allowed in the group settings ✔ Guest Segments — tags are used as one of the filters when creating segments Manual Tag Group List The Manual Tag Group List displays the created groups and their main parameters. To find a group, use the search bar at the top of the page. The search is performed by group name. Manual Tag Group List \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Table Settings Column Wizard \[\[delimiter rows=1]] To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ select the columns to display ✔ pin the required columns ✔ restore the default settings using Reset to Default Note. title: General Information
text: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] What RFM is used for RFM automatically groups guests based on their activity and value to the business. This helps you quickly identify the most loyal guests, those who are beginning to lose interest, and those who need to be re-engaged. Assigned RFM Statuses can be used when working with the guest database, analyzing the audience, and building marketing scenarios. RFM is calculated based on three metrics: ✔ Recency (R) — Number Of Days Since The Last Purchase ✔ Frequency (F) — Average Number Of Checks Per Month Over A Six-Month Period ✔ Monetary (M) — Guest Rating Based On The Amount Spent RFM List \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Each guest is automatically assigned an RFM Status according to the configured segmentation rules. The status determines which category the guest belongs to based on their visit and spending history. In addition to the RFM Status, an RFM Score is calculated for the most valuable guests. It shows the guest's position among guests with the highest metrics and helps identify the most valuable guests within RFM segments. The score is calculated only for the top 1,000 guests. All other guests are assigned only an RFM Status. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] RFM is recalculated automatically once a day. It is also recalculated after an RFM Status is created, changed, or deleted. \[\[/info]] Where RFM is displayed \[\[gallery gap=12 layout=carousel]] Guest List Guest Profile Reservation List \[\[/gallery]] RFM information is displayed in several sections of the system: ✔ Marketing → Guests — the current RFM Status is displayed under each guest's name. ✔ Marketing → Guests — click the required guest and hover over their avatar to view the current RFM Status, RFM Score (if calculated), and status description. ✔ Reservations → Reservation List — RFM is displayed under the guest's name. System Statuses System Statuses \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The system includes two system RFM Statuses that are created automatically. ✔ No Orders — guests who have not yet had any visits or checks. ✔ Unsorted — guests who have had at least one visit but do not meet the conditions of any configured RFM Status. Deactivated guests are also automatically assigned this status. System Status rows are not interactive and cannot be changed or deleted. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Guest List
text: The Guests page displays a list of guests and basic information about each of them. To work with the list, you can select a location or location group, use search and filters, and configure the table columns. Guest List \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Location Selection In the location selector, you can select an individual location, a location group, or All. Location and Filter \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Selecting a location or group does not change the list of guests in the table. It determines which locations are used to display statistics for each guest. If a guest has activity at the selected location, the table displays their metrics for that location, such as the last visit and total amount spent. If there was no activity at the selected location, dashes are displayed in the corresponding columns. The selected location is also taken into account when filtering the list. For example, if you select a specific location and set a filter for the amount spent, the table will show guests whose spending at that location meets the specified condition. For more information about location groups, see Location Groups. Search To find a guest, use the search bar above the table. You can search by first name, last name, primary phone number, email, or loyalty card number. Table Settings To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. Column Wizard \[\[delimiter rows=1]] In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ select the columns to display ✔ pin the required columns ✔ restore the default settings using Reset to Default Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out. Filters If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. Guest Filters \[\[delimiter rows=1]] After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Filter settings are saved after the page is refreshed. The settings are reset after you log out. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Guest Profile
text: Open Guest Profile To open a guest profile: Go to Marketing → Guests Enter one of the following in the search bar: first name, last name, phone number, email address, or loyalty card number Click the required guest in the list to open their profile Guest Profile \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Guest Profile Tabs Guest Profile Tabs \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The guest profile consists of four tabs: ✔ Statistics ✔ Reservations ✔ Orders ✔ Activity Log Note. When the window is narrow, tab names may be replaced with icons. Data Filtering Data Filtering \[\[delimiter rows=1]] To view statistics for a specific location or location group, select the required value from the location dropdown. To change the period used to calculate statistics, select the required period from the period dropdown. After changing the selected values, all metrics and charts on the page are recalculated automatically. Note. The Average Orders Per Month widget uses its own period selection and does not depend on the general page period. Personal Information Colon Button \[\[delimiter rows=1]] To edit the guest's personal information, click the button with the colon icon and select Edit. Make the required changes and click Save. For more information about changing a phone number, see Phone Numbers. Statistics When you open a guest profile, the Statistics tab is displayed by default. It contains information that helps you evaluate the guest's activity, visit history, and preferences. The data is presented as metrics and charts. Guest Profile Top \[\[delimiter rows=1]] 1\. Guest Avatar 2\. Note and Preferences 3\. Loyalty Program 4\. Average Check Per Order 5\. Average Party Size 6\. Avg Check Per Guest 7\. Average Orders Per Month 8\. Autotags and Manual Tags 9\. Visits 10\. Key Indicators Guest Profile Bottom \[\[delimiter rows=1]] 11\. Total Paid 12\. Top Categories 13\. Top Products 14\. Visit Time 1\. Guest Avatar RFM \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Hover over the guest avatar to view the guest's RFM information. The tooltip displays: ✔ current RFM Status ✔ RFM Score, if calculated ✔ a brief description of the current RFM Status For more information, see the RFM page. 2\. Note and Preferences Note \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The Note widget contains two independent fields: ✔ Note — used to store general information about the guest and displayed only in the guest profile ✔ Preferences — used to store the guest's service preferences. They are displayed in the Waiter app and help employees take the guest's preferences into account Click the widget to view or edit both fields. 3\. Loyalty Program Loyalty Account \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The loyalty program widget is located at the top of the guest profile. It displays the balance of the bonus account linked to the loyalty card. Click the widget to open a list of all the guest's bonus accounts. The name and current balance are displayed for each account. If the guest does not participate in the loyalty program, the widget displays No Loyalty Card. 4\. Average Check Per Order Average Check Per Order \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the average value of one guest order. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart shows how the average check changes as orders are placed. 5\. Average Party Size Average Party Size \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the average number of guests per visit. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart shows how the average party size changes as orders are placed. 6\. Avg Check Per Guest Avg Check Per Guest \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the average amount spent by one guest per visit. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The average check is calculated by dividing the total amount of the checks by the total number of guests specified in those checks. 7\. Average Orders Per Month Average Orders Per Month \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the guest's average number of orders per month. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations. The widget uses its own period selection, independent of the general page period. The chart displays: a solid line — data for the selected period a dashed line — data for the previous equivalent period Note. Full calendar periods are used for the calculation. For example, Last Month means the last full calendar month, not the last 30 days. 8\. Tags Tags Widget \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The Tags widget displays Autotags and Manual Tags assigned to the guest. Hover over a tag to view its full name and description, if provided. To add Manual Tags, click the edit icon next to the Manual Tags field. In the window that opens, select the required tags. For more information, see the Manual Tags and Autotags pages. 9\. Visits Visits \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The widget displays information about the guest's visits. The data is calculated based on closed checks and cancelled reservations. The following information is displayed: ✔ total number of visits ✔ number of cancelled reservations ✔ date of the last visit ✔ percentage of visits and cancellations Note. The number of visits is calculated for all time and does not depend on the selected period. 10\. Key Indicators Key Indicators \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the guest's key indicators for the selected period. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The following indicators are displayed: Total Paid Discount Checks Count Last Check Avg Check Avg Check Per Hour Avg Time Favorite Location The radial chart displays the relative values of the following indicators compared with other guests at the selected locations: ✔ Total Paid ✔ Discount ✔ Avg Check ✔ Avg Check Per Hour ✔ Avg Time When you hover over a point on the chart, the guest's position relative to other guests is displayed. For example: "The guest has higher Average Check than 39% of other guests." The value depends on the selected period and is recalculated when the period changes. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] For Avg Check Per Hour, only checks that meet at least one of the following conditions are included: ✔ check duration is at least 30 minutes ✔ check total is at least 50 AED for the UAE or 1,000 RUB for Russia \[\[/info]] 11\. Total Paid Total Paid \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the guest's check totals in chronological order for the selected period. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart displays: X-axis — the sequence of checks Y-axis — the total amount of each check In Last 30 Checks mode, individual checks are displayed as points on the chart. Hover over a point to view: ✔ Location ✔ Check Date ✔ Visit Start and End Time ✔ Visit Duration ✔ Check Total Click a point to open the order details. 12\. Top Categories Top Categories \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the three product categories with the highest total sales at the selected locations for the selected period. For each category, the following information is displayed: ✔ category name ✔ total sales ✔ number of items sold Note. Only categories with Guest Stats enabled in the Menu section are included in the calculation. The chart displays: X-axis — the sequence of checks Y-axis — the category sales amount in each check 13\. Top Products Top Products \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the five products with the highest total sales at the selected locations for the selected period. For each product, the following information is displayed: ✔ product name ✔ total sales ✔ number of items sold ✔ modifiers Hover over the modifiers to view a list of all modifiers and their quantities. 14\. Visit Time Visit Time \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displays the start and end times of the guest's visits for the selected period. The calculation is based on closed checks at the selected locations for the selected period. The chart displays: X-axis — the sequence of checks Y-axis — time of day the start and end time of each visit visit duration as the area between the lines In Last 30 Checks mode, hover over a visit to view: ✔ location ✔ visit date ✔ start and end time ✔ visit duration ✔ check total Click a visit marker to open the order details. Blacklist Colon Button \[\[delimiter rows=1]] To add a guest to the blacklist, click the button with the colon icon and select Add to Blacklist. Blacklist \[\[delimiter rows=1]] When adding a guest to the blacklist, specify the reason and duration: Forever Until Date To remove a guest from the blacklist, click the button with the colon icon, select Remove from Blacklist, specify the reason, and confirm the action. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Multi-Table Reservation
text: Multi-table reservation is a reservation for 2 or more tables. This type of reservation has its own peculiarities and limitations, which we will discuss below. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] When creating a reservation for multiple tables, there should be no time gaps between all tables. The system will show itself if there is a time gap between tables in one reservation. Selecting Multiple Tables via Sidebar \[\[delimiter rows=1]] 1\. Open the table list. 2\. Select the required tables, then click Apply. Selecting Multiple Tables via Timeline 1\. Open the section Timeline. 2\. title: Processing Reservation Request
text: Basic information about the request entity is described in this article. Here we describe how to process requests and all possible interactions with them. How to Process a Request \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Three main actions are available for an active request: Reject; Make a reservation; Open guest profile, if found in the system. Converting a Request to a Reservation Open the request. Click Confirm. If the guest was not previously in the system, fill in and confirm the new guest data. Check the visit date and time, specify the duration. Check the number of guests. Select one or more tables. Check the comment. Check or create guest profile. Save the reservation. After saving, the request receives the status Converted to reservation. The new reservation appears on the timeline, floor plan and reservations table according to standard rules. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Before saving, check the availability of the selected time and tables. When submitting a request, the guest can select any 15-minute interval available in the widget without taking into account the current occupancy of the establishment. The set of available intervals is determined by the location's operating hours. \[\[/info]] Rejecting a Request Reject the request if the establishment cannot accept the request or the guest declined the visit. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Open the request. Click Reject. Select a reason. Confirm the action. Available reasons: No available seats; Cancelled by guest; Undesirable guest; Error; Technical reasons. After rejection, the request receives the status Rejected. It is no longer displayed among active requests on the timeline and floor plan. In the table, the record is retained for viewing, but actions with it become unavailable. Opening Guest Profile The button to go to the profile is available if the system found the guest by phone number and linked them to the request. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Open the request. Click on the guest's name or the profile transition button. View or supplement the guest data. If the profile is not found, the request displays the data entered in the form. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Guest Tags from Widget If manual guest tag selection is configured in the widget, their application depends on whether the profile is found. If the guest is found, selected tags are applied to their profile. If the guest is not found, tags are saved inside the request. Deferred tags are applied after creating the guest profile when converting the request to a reservation. Before creating a profile, tags from the request are not applied to the guest. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Notifications If corresponding templates are configured in reservation settings, the system can send messages to guests for events: Request creation; Request rejection. \[\[delimiter rows=3]] Read further: — Reservation Requests \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Description of reservation request processing functionality via external services

title: Publishing and Distributing a Survey
text: After creation, a survey is saved as a draft. For respondents to be able to complete it, the survey must be published. After the first publication, the system creates a permanent public link and makes the survey available for connecting to mailings. Publishing a Survey \[\[delimiter rows=1]] A survey with the status Draft or Unpublished can be published. Open the survey. Check its structure and settings. Specify the survey completion period (applies to personal links, more on this below) Click Publish. Confirm publication in the modal window. When publishing, the system saves the current changes and validates the form. Upon successful publication: The status changes to Published; A public link is created upon first publication; The survey becomes available for selection in mailings. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Upon republishing, a new public link is not created. The system reactivates the link generated at the first publication. \[\[/info]] Public Link The public link is intended for open completion of the survey without being tied to a specific guest. Features: Suitable for a QR code, website, social networks and other open channels; Responses can be sent via one public link with no limit on the number of completions; If the survey is unpublished or deactivated, the public link becomes unavailable for completion and copying. Personal Link A personal link is generated for a specific guest when the survey is sent via a mailing. Through it, the system can link the received response to the guest's profile. Features: A response can be submitted via one link only once; The link has a limited validity period. Survey Completion Period The Survey completion period parameter determines how long the personal link remains valid from the moment the message is sent. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The default is 3 days. If you change the completion period, the new value applies to all personal links for this survey, including those already sent. \[\[/info]] After the period expires, the respondent will see a message that the survey is unavailable. Sending a Survey via Mailing To add a survey to a mailing message: Open the creation or editing of a mailing in the Marketing -> Mailings section. At the Content step, add the Survey link variable to the message text. In the Related survey field, select the required survey. Save the mailing settings. The Related survey field is required. The list displays only published surveys. When sending, the system generates a personal link for each recipient. Additionally, the system checks: The guest must not be unsubscribed from survey mailings; For an automatic mailing with the Closed check trigger, the survey's location must match the order's location. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] In the current implementation, the response location is determined automatically only for responses received from an automatic mailing with the Closed check trigger. For other methods of receiving a response, the location field may be empty. \[\[/info]] Related Mailings The Distribution tab displays a block of related mailings. For each mailing, its name and current status are shown. This allows you to see where the current survey is being used. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Unpublishing a Survey A survey with the status Published can be unpublished. Open the published survey. Click Unpublish. Confirm the action. After confirmation: The status changes to Unpublished; The public link stops working; The survey becomes unavailable for new connections in mailings; Active mailings using this survey are switched to the status Paused. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Unpublishing does not save the current unsaved changes to the form. Save your changes before performing this action. \[\[/info]] Republishing An unpublished survey can be published again. Republishing follows the same steps as the initial publication. In this case, the previous public link is used. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Related mailings previously switched to the status Paused are not automatically resumed. They must be activated separately. \[\[/info]]

title: Reservation Requests
text: Reservation requests help you process guest requests sent through a website widget or supported external reservation service. A request captures the desired date, time and visit parameters, but does not automatically reserve a table. For the request to become a reservation, an employee must check the data and confirm it manually. You can work with requests in all views of the Reservations section: on the timeline, floor plan and a separate requests table. Brief Work Scenario Guest submits a form in the widget on the website or external reservation service. The request appears in the Reservations section. An employee opens the request, checks the data and contacts the guest if necessary. The request can be: Accepted and converted to a reservation Rejected After confirmation, the table is reserved with a standard reservation. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] A request and a reservation are different entities. Until the request is converted to a reservation, the selected time is not considered occupied and the table is not reserved. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=1]] How a request is created: A request is created manually by a guest through a reservations widget. The system links the request to an existing profile if the guest is found. Saves the data inside the request if the guest is not found. Passes the request to the Reservations section for manual processing by an employee. A new guest profile is not created automatically at this stage. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Displaying and Working with Requests You can work with requests in all views of the Reservations section. When a new request arrives, the counter of the Requests button increases. It shows the number of requests with New status or requests being processed. Requests in Table \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Go to the Reservations section. Go to the Requests tab. Click on the row to open the request sidebar. The table displays: Desired visit date and time; Guest or name specified in the form; Tags selected in the widget; Phone number; Number of guests; Status; Comment; Time the request has been in New status. Search, filtering and sorting: In the table you can search requests by first name, last name and phone number. Filtering is available by visit date, guest, request status and comment text. By default, requests are sorted: By date and time of desired visit — from closest to later ones. By processing wait time — first requests that have been in New status longer. Requests with Rejected status are not displayed unless explicitly specified in the filter. This sorting helps you process the closest and longest-waiting requests first (it is important to set the current status first). \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] In the requests table you can also create a reservation by clicking the + button in the lower right part of the section. \[\[/info]] Statistics: At the bottom of the table, statistics on requests are displayed. Total count and by all statuses for the selected day. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Requests on Timeline Go to the Reservations section. Open the Timeline view. Click Requests. In the opened sidebar, select the required card. Requests on Floor Plan \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Go to the Reservations section. Open the Floor Plan view. In the sidebar switch from the Reservations tab to Requests. Select a request. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] A request is not displayed on the floor plan as an occupied table. The table will be marked as occupied only after the request is converted to a reservation. \[\[/info]] Unlike other views, a system guest is immediately available here if linked to the request. Other data is pulled from the request. Request Card The request card displays: Guest name specified in the form; Phone number; Desired visit date and time; Number of guests; Comment; Time elapsed since the request was created. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] After opening the card, processing actions become available. Original request data cannot be changed, but a reservation can be created based on them. \[\[/info]] Request Statuses \[\[delimiter rows=1]] A request can have the following statuses: New — request has entered the system, but the employee has not yet taken action. Rejected — employee declined the request. Converted to reservation — a reservation has been created based on the request. Processing mark — the request is currently being opened or edited by an employee (status is indicated by an edit icon). Rejected and Converted to reservation statuses are final. After transitioning to one of them, the request is no longer considered active. Enabling New Request Notifications \[\[delimiter rows=1]] In the Reservations section click on your avatar to open the action menu. Select Enable notifications. Allow Show notifications in the popup window in the browser. Check that notifications are enabled in your browser's system settings. \[\[delimiter rows=3]] Read further: — Processing Reservation Request \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Description of reservation request functionality via external services

title: Reservation Statuses
text: Status shows the current state of a reservation: whether it is confirmed, if the guest is in the establishment or the reservation was cancelled. You can specify the status in the sidebar when creating or editing a reservation. Five reservation statuses are provided: Not confirmed Confirmed In progress Completed Cancelled \[\[delimiter rows=1]] \[\[info type=custom hasIcon icon=info color=#E06823]] Statuses Cancelled and Completed are only available when editing a reservation. \[\[/info]] INDICATORS AND ALERTS The color of the reservation card helps quickly determine its current status. Color Indicators on Timeline: Yellow — status "Confirmed" Orange — status "Not confirmed" Green — status "In progress" Dark green — status "Completed" Pink — status "Not confirmed", if guest is late Light blue — status "Confirmed", if guest is late Red — status "Cancelled" Color Indicators on Floor Plan: Yellow — status "Confirmed" Orange — status "Not confirmed" Green — status "In progress" Pink — status "Not confirmed", if guest is late Light blue — status "Confirmed", if guest is late Additional Alerts: Text alerts for late arrival — displayed on the reservation card on the timeline from the first minute of guest delay. Text alerts for reservation end — shows how much time remains until the end of the guest's visit. \[\[delimiter rows=3]] Read further: — Creating a Reservation \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Description of reservation statuses

title: Reservation Tags
text: Reservation tags help you manually mark reservations within the CRM. With their help you can visually highlight important records, quickly understand the context of a reservation, group reservations and find them using filters. For example, you can create tags Needs parking, Late arrival, High priority or Requires manager attention. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Reservation tags are not related to guest tags. These are separate types of tags that are configured and used independently of each other. \[\[/info]] Tag List In the section Reservations -> Reservation Tags a list of created tags and basic information about them is displayed. In this section you can view, create and edit tags. Search, filtering and sorting Search: by Name field — search begins after entering at least three characters. Filtering: by Locations, Creation/Update Date, Author. Sorting: by name, short name, creation date or last update date. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Creating a Tag 1\. Open the section Reservations -> Reservation Tags. 2\. Click Create. 3\. Fill in the fields: Locations — when adding a tag to a reservation, the system shows only tags available for the selected location Name Short name — abbreviation that is displayed on the reservation Tooltip text — displayed when hovering over the tag Description Color Icon 4\. If necessary, add a description, icon and tooltip text. 5\. Click Save. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] After saving, the tag will appear in the general tag list and will be available in the tag list when editing a reservation. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Editing a Tag In an existing tag you can edit all fields. After saving changes apply to all reservations that use the tag. Before saving, the system warns that the change may affect related reservations. Details of tag changes and creation can be seen inside the tag card. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Deleting a Tag Open the section Reservations -> Reservation Tags. Find the required tag. Click on the tag, opening editing. Click Delete. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Confirm deletion. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] After deletion: The tag will completely disappear from the system; The tag will be removed from all associated reservations; The tag will become unavailable for assignment and filtering; The change log of reservations where this tag was previously specified will not change. Using Tags in Reservations Adding a Tag Multiple tags can be assigned to one reservation. Only tags available for the location of this reservation are displayed in the list. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Open the required reservation. Click Add tag. Find the tag by name or select it from the list. If necessary, select other tags. Click Save. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] After saving, the selected tags will be associated with the reservation and appear in its side panel. \[\[/info]] Removing a Tag from a Reservation Open the reservation. Click the delete icon next to the tag. Click Save. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] The tag will be removed only from the selected reservation. The tag itself will remain available in the system and will continue to be used in other reservations. \[\[/info]] Change History The system saves actions with tags in the reservation history. The time and author of tag addition or removal can be seen in the Change Log. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Filtering Reservations by Tags Open the section Reservations. Go to table display mode. Open the filter by tags. Select one or more tags. The table will show only reservations matching the selected conditions. Tags of the selected location are available for filtering. \[\[delimiter rows=1]]

title: Reservation Timeline
text: The module has three display modes for reservations. Each one is suitable for different tasks: working with reservations, analyzing occupancy and managing guest seating. Timeline Floor Plan Table Timeline Timeline is an area with a time scale on which all reservations are displayed. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Main elements: List of floors and tables (Floors can be collapsed and expanded). Time scale with reservations. Button to create a reservation. Statistics of completed reservations for the day. Information on reservations on the selected floor (Colors correspond to status model) Transition to canceled reservations in Archive. Creating a Reservation on Timeline You can create a reservation directly on the timeline in several ways: Single click opens a sidebar to create a reservation. Click and drag right or left allow you to immediately set the reservation duration. Drag up or down allows you to select multiple tables at once (more about multi-reservation). \[\[delimiter rows=1]] \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] You can also create a reservation via the Reservation creation button in the lower right corner. More about ways to create a reservation — in article. \[\[/info]] Table List When you select a table, information about it is displayed: Layout and maximum capacity. Tags. Deposits and exclusions. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] In this same window you can add a block on a table for the selected period. During a block the table will be unavailable for reservations. \[\[/info]] To block a table you need to specify: One or more tables. Block start time and duration. Reason for blocking. Floor Plan Floor plan is a visual representation of the establishment's tables, which allows you to assess the hall occupancy and manage reservations tied to specific tables. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] More about the floor plan in this article. Table Display of Reservations In this mode, reservations are displayed as a table. Records can be sorted and filtered. Also, a summary of reservations is displayed in the section taking into account the applied filters. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Page elements: Button to refresh table data. Setting of displayed columns. Summary of reservations based on selected filters. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Data in the table does not update automatically. If the data has changed, the update button will notify you. To load current information, click Refresh. \[\[/info]] \[\[delimiter rows=3]] Read further: — Floor Plan — Creating a Reservation \[\[delimiter rows=3]]
description: Navigation and functionality of the Timeline

title: Reservations
text: \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The Reservations tab contains a list of all reservations associated with the selected guest. Here you can view the reservation history, including active, completed, and cancelled reservations. Reservation List \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Reservation Summary Click Summary at the bottom of the window. Reservation Summary \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Cancelled Reservations Summary \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Use the Active / Cancelled switch to view a summary of active and cancelled reservations. For active reservations, the data is grouped by status; for cancelled reservations, by cancellation reason. The Guests row shows the number of guests in the reservations, while the Reservations row shows the number of reservations. Note. The summary is calculated based on all reservations matching the selected filters. Table Management Column Selection \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The table displays information about the selected guest's reservations. To change the displayed columns, click the table settings button in the upper-right corner. In the panel that opens, you can: ✔ select the columns to display ✔ pin the required columns ✔ restore the default settings using Reset to Default Note. Table settings are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The settings are reset after you log out. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Data Filtering Reservations with Filters \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Select the required location from the list to display only reservations associated with that location. To change the displayed period, select the required date range. If necessary, click Filters to set additional filtering conditions. After selecting the required values, click Apply. Applied filters are displayed above the table. To remove an individual filter, click × next to its name. To reset all filters, click Clear Filters. Note. Selected filter values are saved after the page is refreshed and when switching between guest profiles. The filters are reset after you log out. \[\[delimiter rows=3]]

title: Responses and Working with Responses
text: The Responses section is used for viewing and analyzing survey results. Responses can be opened within a specific survey or in the general table across all available surveys. Within a survey, only responses for that survey are displayed. The general Responses table displays responses for all surveys available to you. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Basic Response Data The table can display the following data: Response number Response date — date and time the response was submitted by the respondent. Survey name Location — the location associated with the response. Automatically determined for responses from an automatic mailing based on the Closed check trigger; in other cases it may be absent. Response source — shows how the response entered the system: Mailing, Public link or Entered manually. Channel — delivery channel, if the survey was sent via mailing. For a public link and manual entry, the field may be empty. Added by — for a manual response, shows the employee who entered the data. Text responses — the number of text comments in the response, including text in the Custom option field. Ratings — ratings left in Rating type questions. Device — Mobile or Computer, depending on the device from which the response was submitted. For responses received after an automatic mailing, the following may be displayed: Trigger — the event after which the mailing was sent; Trigger date — date and time of the event; Tables — tables associated with the event; Served by — employees who served the guest. If the response is linked to a guest profile, the following may be displayed: First and Last Name; Phone; Email; Gender; Date of birth. Response Filters Period The Period filter limits responses by the date they were received. The maximum date is the current day. Depending on the available data, responses can be filtered by the following parameters: Trigger date Response source Channel Who added — the employee who added the manual response, or the system; Served by — the employee associated with the event; Ratings — a range of rating values; if a response has several ratings, a match on at least one is sufficient; Tables Has text responses Device In the general table, the following are additionally available: Locations — including the option No location; Survey — filter by survey name. The list includes published and unpublished surveys; drafts are not displayed. Viewing a Response To open detailed information, click on the response row. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] The details window may display: Response number; Guest and their phone number; Location; Survey name; Date and time of response; Response source; Employee who added the manual response; Device; Check number, if the response is linked to a check; Tables; Employees who served the guest; Answers to the survey questions. Adding a Response Manually Manual addition is used when an employee conducts a survey on behalf of a guest, for example over the phone. \[\[delimiter rows=1]] Open the general Responses table. Click Add response. Select a Location. The list displays locations available to you. Select a Survey. Before selecting a location, this field is unavailable. The list displays only published surveys for the selected location. Enter the guest's primary phone number. Click Add response. If an active guest profile is found, the system will open the selected survey. Complete the survey on behalf of the guest and submit the answers. After submission, the system creates a new response and links it to the selected location, survey and guest. The source Entered manually is set for such a response. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] If an active guest profile is not found by the specified phone number, the system will show an error and will not allow starting the survey. \[\[/info]] Deleting a Response \[\[delimiter rows=1]] To delete a response: Find and select the response in the table. Select the action Delete. Confirm the deletion. After deletion, the response receives the system status Deleted and is no longer used in working data. The system also reduces the number of responses for the survey and recalculates related guest metrics, auto-tags and segments. \[\[info type=custom color=#E06823]] Deleting a response does not make the personal link available for retaking. When this link is opened again, the respondent will still see a message that the survey has already been completed. \[\[/info]]
description: Viewing, filtering, manually adding and deleting survey responses.
